transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The Federal Reserve has decided to keep interest rates steady for now.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the central bank is still expected to raise rates later this year
as it tries to curb stubborn inflation.
Consumer prices are still climbing much faster than the Federal Reserve would like,
partly as a result of the U.S. war with Iran, which has triggered a spike in energy prices.
The central bank raised its benchmark interest rate last month in an effort to tamp down demand
and slow those price hikes, but any additional rate hikes are on hold for now.
The Fed's rate-setting committee voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark rate where it is.
The two dissenters would have preferred to raise rates by a quarter percentage point.
The decision comes less than a week before votes are tallied in the midterm election.
President Trump has aggressively lobbied the Fed to lower interest rates.
Polls show nearly two-thirds of the public disapproves to the President's handling of the economy.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Well, the White House says President Trump will showcase record results when he returns today to the Buckeye State.
In a press release, it touts major tax breaks as well as job and wage protections.
The latest NPR/PBS news merest poll finds though a majority of voters surveyed disagree
that Trump has done a good job with the economy.
Minnesota is charging two conservative influencers with voter fraud.
Today, Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said James O'Keefe and Cameron Higby
committed felonies through unlawful voting and identity theft.
Moriarty says they filmed themselves using the names of registered voters for a YouTube video
reporting to test the state's vouching rules during Minnesota's August 11th primary.
Mr. O'Keefe and Mr. Higby entered polling places in multiple instances,
identified themselves using names of registered voters in those precincts
without those voters' knowledge or permission.
Minnesota Public Radio reports that O'Keefe's group issued a press release in August
saying the people in the video did not cast ballots.
But Moriarty says it's still a state crime to intentionally misrepresent one's identity
in applying for a ballot even if a voter oath to receive a ballot has not been signed.
Affordable housing is a key issue for many voters.
NPR's Jennifer Lutton reports it's also motivating Gen Z candidates in state house races.
In Montana, 21-year-old Republican Lucas Schubert wants to create more starter homes
young people can afford to buy.
That has been one of the biggest factors in development for the middle class in this country.
In New Haven, Connecticut, 26-year-old Democrat Eli Saban is a renter
unlike the vast majority of elected officials and says that makes a difference.
I think it's the experience of being a renter
and just the insecurity and instability that you feel.
28-year-old Democrat Olalea Anukuyade in Hartford appreciates the national conversation on housing.
But the action is happening at the state level.
Jennifer Lutton, NPR News.
This is NPR.
U.S. Southern Command killed five people in a small boat transiting the Eastern Pacific.
More from NPR's Quill Lawrence.
U.S. Southern Command released a grainy targeting video on social media
showing a motionless boat with a small crew exploding in flames.
Southcom claimed those aboard were narco traffickers.
That's how the U.S. military has justified killing nearly 250 people since September of last year.
In at least one case, Southcom made a second strike to kill shipwrecked survivors.
Some American allies have stopped sharing intelligence with the U.S. on drug smuggling
because it's against the law to kill suspects without trial
and against the laws of war to kill unarmed people who show no hostile intent.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
The French soccer star Killian Mbappe has issued an apology.
Following a comment about the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong,
NPR's Jennifer Pack reports at least three Chinese companies
have severed their brand deals with him.
Mbappe says his comment was ill-judged and hurt many people in China.
It all started when Mbappe told a French talk show
there was a funny meme where his face was photoshopped on Mao,
which Mbappe referred to as "some guy I think he's a Chinese dictator."
Mao is officially revered as the founding father of modern China.
Economic repercussions are common in China for perceived slights.
CCTV will not show Real Madrid's next match, just like they did in 2019
when they stopped airing NBA games for a whole year.
It happened after the Houston Rockets general manager
tweeted support for anti-government protesters in Hong Kong.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
It's NPR.

topics.text: The Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady, voting 10-2 amid stubborn inflation tied to the Iran war
President Trump heads to Ohio to tout economic results; NPR/PBS poll finds majority disapprove of his economic handling
Minnesota charges conservative influencers James O'Keefe and Cameron Higby with voter fraud over primary polling place stunt
NPR's Jennifer Lutton reports Gen Z state house candidates in Montana, Connecticut, and Hartford campaigning on housing affordability
U.S. Southern Command kills five people on a small boat in the Eastern Pacific, part of nearly 250 such deaths
French soccer star Kylian Mbappe apologizes after comparing Mao Zedong to a dictator, prompting Chinese brand deals to end
CCTV reportedly will not air Real Madrid's next match following Mbappe's comments about Mao
